name: FActScore
executive_summary: Decomposes long-form text into atomic facts and verifies each one independently, producing a granular factuality score for the entire generation.
description: FActScore addresses the challenge of evaluating long-form factuality by breaking text into atomic, verifiable claims. Each claim is checked against a knowledge source. The ratio of supported facts to total facts yields the FActScore.
when_to_use: When you need to localize which specific claims are hallucinated.
Benchmarking model factuality with a fine-grained metric.
when_not_to_use: When no verification source is available.
Creative writing where factual claims are intentionally fictional.
known_pitfalls: Atomic fact decomposition itself can be error-prone.
Verification source may be incomplete or outdated.
Cost scales with the number of atomic facts.

primary_source.authors: Min, Krishna, Lyu, Lewis, Yih, Koh, Iyyer, Zettlemoyer, Hajishirzi
primary_source.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation

variables.name: text
variables.example: Albert Einstein was born in Germany in 1879. He developed the theory of relativity...

variables.name: atomic_facts
variables.example: ["Albert Einstein was born in Germany.", "Albert Einstein was born in 1879.", "Albert Einstein developed the theory of relativity."]

variables.name: overall_score
variables.description: Ratio of supported facts to total facts.

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: Decomposition and verification are typically deterministic. Score may vary slightly based on verification source coverage.
